## Example files

Build your own file. Use these examples to check a step when you are stuck, then return to your work. Do not submit the example files. Select the lesson object; press Home over the node editor to see the graph. Follow the Frames in order. Change inputs on the nodes or, where provided, in the GeometryNodes modifier.

Prepared in **Blender 5.2.1 LTS**. Earlier Blender versions may lack the volume nodes used in the later classes.

**[Arrays — Part 1: linear and nested grid]({{ site.baseurl }}/files/blender/03-arrays-lists/Arrays-Lists-Session-1.blend)** — download .blend

1. Linear loop
2. Nested grid

**[Arrays — Part 2: arrangements and rules]({{ site.baseurl }}/files/blender/03-arrays-lists/Arrays-Lists-Session-2.blend)** — download .blend

1. 3D array
2. Hexagonal array
3. Radial array
4. If and range
5. Sine curve

Before hexagonal arrays, the simple 3D array repeats a row into a grid and a grid into layers; Count, Spacing and Cube Size remain exposed. The last scene, Sine curve, uses math along X and Y and repetition in three dimensions to shape a volume of cubes. It introduces the later density and signed-distance lessons while retaining cube instances.

**Practice:** Practice with your P3a module. Sheet 1 of P3b: 1D, 2D and 3D arrays (compare 3, 4 and 5 copies per axis in the cube). Sheet 2: hexagonal, radial and curve arrays.
